children.title: Nonglobal Local Minima
children.top_down_role: Covers convergence outcomes at locally minimizing points that are not globally optimal.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonglobal Local Minima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local minimizers whose objective value exceeds the global infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and let \(F:X\to\mathbb{R}\). A point \(x_*\in X\) is a nonglobal local minimum if there exists \(\delta>0\) such that
\[F(x_*)\le F(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in X\cap B_\delta(x_*),\]
but
\[F(x_*)>\inf_{x\in X}F(x).\]
If the global infimum is attained, the second condition is equivalent to the existence of \(y\in X\) satisfying \(F(y)<F(x_*)\). The definition applies directly to residual objectives such as \(F(x)=\tfrac12\|r(x)\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonglobal local minimum is optimal within some neighborhood but has strictly larger objective value than the best feasible value.

notation.meaning: Open Euclidean ball of radius delta about the candidate point

children.title: Basin-of-Attraction Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Covers dependence of the attained solution on attraction-region boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Basin-of-Attraction Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instability of an algorithmic attractor under arbitrarily small initialization perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:X\to X\) be an iteration map on a metric space \((X,d)\), and let \(a\) be an attracting fixed point with basin
\[\mathcal B(a)=\{x\in X:T^k(x)\to a\}.\]
The outcome is basin-sensitive at \(x_0\in\overline{\mathcal B(a)}\) if, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist \(u,v\in X\) with \(d(u,x_0)<\varepsilon\) and \(d(v,x_0)<\varepsilon\) such that \(u\in\mathcal B(a)\) while \(v\in\mathcal B(b)\) for some attractor \(b\ne a\), or \(T^k(v)\) fails to converge. Thus no neighborhood of \(x_0\) has a unique asymptotic outcome.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basin sensitivity means arbitrarily close starting points can converge to different attractors, or one can converge while the other does not.
assumptions_latex: \(T:X\to X\) has an attracting fixed point \(a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every neighborhood of \(x_0\) contains initializations with distinct asymptotic outcomes.

notation.meaning: Basin of attraction of the fixed point
k-fold iterate of the update map

children.title: Initialization-Dependent Outcomes
children.top_down_role: Covers variation in terminal outcomes caused by starting-point selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Initialization-Dependent Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of an iterative solver's limiting result on its starting point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let an algorithm with fixed data and fixed hyperparameters define iterates \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\) on \(X\). Its outcome is initialization-dependent on \(D\subseteq X\) if there exist \(x_0,y_0\in D\) for which both limits exist and
\[x_\infty(x_0)=\lim_{k\to\infty}T^k(x_0),\qquad x_\infty(y_0)=\lim_{k\to\infty}T^k(y_0),\qquad x_\infty(x_0)\ne x_\infty(y_0),\]
or exactly one of the two sequences converges. If both limits are feasible stationary points with unequal objective values, initialization changes not only the returned point but also the attained solution quality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With data and solver settings fixed, different initial points produce different limits, or produce convergence for one run and failure for another.
assumptions_latex: The update map \(T\) and all noninitial inputs are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The asymptotic outcome map is not constant on \(D\), or convergence status differs on \(D\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property correctly formalizes dependence on initialization with all other algorithmic inputs fixed. An inspectable convergence or dynamical-systems source is required before retaining the interpretation as candidate-review knowledge.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual contamination and model-misspecification boundary
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let observations satisfy \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\), let \(h:\Theta\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be a model family, and define \(r(\theta)=y-h(\theta)\). Let \(\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be a declared contamination class and \(\mathcal{E}_\delta=\{e:\|e\|\le\delta\}\) an admissible ordinary-error set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic residual decomposition. The boundary is relative to specified contamination, noise, and model classes; without these classes contamination and misspecification are not identifiable from a residual alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The data are contamination-compatible at level \(\delta\) when \[\exists\theta\in\Theta,\ c\in\mathcal{C},\ e\in\mathcal{E}_\delta:\quad y=h(\theta)+c+e.\] They are clean-model compatible when the same condition holds with \(c=0\). They are misspecified relative to \((h,\mathcal{C},\delta)\) when \[d(y,\mathcal{H}+\mathcal{C})=\inf_{\theta,c}\|y-h(\theta)-c\|>\delta,\] where \(\mathcal{H}=h(\Theta)\). The contamination–misspecification boundary is the level set \(d(y,\mathcal{H}+\mathcal{C})=\delta\). Decompositional ambiguity occurs when both clean and nonzero-contamination representations exist or when distinct pairs \((\theta,c)\) fit within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given explicit model, contamination, and ordinary-error classes, observations are contamination-compatible if they can be represented as a model prediction plus an allowed contamination vector and bounded ordinary error. They are misspecified if even the enlarged model-plus-contamination class cannot approach the data within tolerance. The boundary is the distance level set equal to the tolerance. Multiple admissible decompositions represent ambiguity rather than a uniquely diagnosed cause.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[y\text{ is misspecified}\iff d(y,\mathcal{H}+\mathcal{C})>\delta,\qquad y\text{ is on the boundary}\iff d(y,\mathcal{H}+\mathcal{C})=\delta.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Compatibility is equivalent to \(y\in\mathcal{H}+\mathcal{C}+\mathcal{E}_\delta\).
For \(\delta=0\), exact contamination compatibility is membership in the Minkowski sum \(\mathcal{H}+\mathcal{C}\).
special_cases_latex: Sparse contamination uses \(\mathcal{C}=\{c:\|c\|_0\le s\}\) or a bounded version of that set.
With \(\mathcal{C}=\{0\}\), the boundary reduces to the ordinary model-adequacy boundary \(d(y,\mathcal{H})=\delta\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Residual magnitude alone cannot distinguish contamination from misspecification.
Enlarging \(\mathcal{C}\) weakens the misspecification diagnosis and can increase decomposition ambiguity.
boundary_notes: The definition is deterministic and does not assign probabilities to contamination or noise.
If the contamination class is unrestricted, every datum is contamination-compatible and the distinction becomes vacuous.

notation.meaning: Distance from the observations to the augmented model class.

review_flags: No inspected robust-estimation or model-misspecification source supports this exact set-distance definition.
The contamination class and ambiguity clauses require source validation.

children.title: Outlier-Driven Residual Distortion
children.top_down_role: Covers residual landscapes dominated by atypical or contaminated observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Outlier-Driven Residual Distortion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A single-contamination family showing unbounded displacement under squared-residual fitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For scalar location data \(y_1=\cdots=y_{n-1}=0\) and \(y_n=M\), consider the least-squares residual objective
\[F_M(\theta)=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n(y_i-\theta)^2.\]
Its unique minimizer is \(\widehat\theta_M=M/n\). Therefore one contaminated observation drives \(|\widehat\theta_M|\to\infty\) as \(|M|\to\infty\), even though the uncontaminated observations remain fixed. At the minimizer, the ordinary residuals are \(-M/n\) for each clean observation and \(M(1-1/n)\) for the outlier, so contamination distorts both the estimate and the entire residual pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In least-squares location fitting, one arbitrarily large outlier moves the estimate without bound and induces nonzero residuals on every clean observation.
assumptions_latex: The loss is unweighted squared residual loss.
Exactly one observation equals \(M\), while the others equal zero.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample and residual calculations are correct, and counterexample is the appropriate mathematical role for this leaf. A robust-statistics source with a specific locator is required to support the contamination interpretation.

children.title: Structural Model Misspecification
children.top_down_role: Covers residual mismatch caused by an inadequate model family.

knowledge_statements.title: Structural Model Misspecification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent population residual discrepancy caused by positive separation of the data-generating conditional mean from the model class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y=g_0(X)+\varepsilon\), where \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon\mid X]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon^2]<\infty\), and let \(\mathcal G=\{g(\cdot;\theta):\theta\in\Theta\}\subset L^2(P_X)\) be the fitted response family. The model is structurally misspecified with a positive approximation gap for the conditional mean if
\[\delta_*^2:=\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\mathbb E\!\left[(g_0(X)-g(X;\theta))^2\right]>0.\]
If \(\theta_*\) attains this infimum, then the systematic residual component \(b(X)=g_0(X)-g(X;\theta_*)\) is nonzero in \(L^2(P_X)\). Consequently, neither increasing the sample size nor solving the fitting problem more accurately can eliminate the positive population approximation gap while the response family remains \(\mathcal G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structural misspecification with a positive approximation gap occurs when the true conditional mean remains a strictly positive L2 distance from every response available in the chosen model family.
assumptions_latex: \(g_0\) and every member of \(\mathcal G\) belong to \(L^2(P_X)\).
A parameter \(\theta_*\) attaining the infimum exists when \(b\) is invoked.

notation.meaning: Systematic residual component at an attaining parameter

children.title: Contamination versus Misspecification
children.top_down_role: Covers ambiguity between observation-level contamination and systematic model inadequacy.

knowledge_statements.title: Contamination versus Misspecification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An observational nonuniqueness boundary between sparse corruption and systematic model discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given design points \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), observations \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_n)^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^n\), a data-generating response \(g_0\), and a fitted model \(g(x;\theta)\), define \(g_0^n=(g_0(x_i))_{i=1}^n\) and \(g_\theta=(g(x_i;\theta))_{i=1}^n\). Suppose
\[y=g_0^n+c+e,\]
where \(c\in\mathbb R^n\) is observation contamination and \(e\in\mathbb R^n\) is ordinary noise. The fitted residual is then
\[r(\theta)=y-g_\theta=c+b(\theta)+e,\qquad b(\theta)=g_0^n-g_\theta.\]
Without identifying restrictions on \(c\) and \(b(\theta)\), their allocation is not identifiable from the residual: for every \(d\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[c+b(\theta)=(c+d)+(b(\theta)-d).\]
Consequently, separating contamination from misspecification requires additional assumptions, such as sparsity of \(c\), regularity or low complexity of \(b(\theta)\), and sufficient design information; residual magnitude alone cannot determine the cause.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without additional restrictions, the observed residual cannot distinguish contamination from model discrepancy because the same residual component admits infinitely many allocations between those two causes.
assumptions_latex: No identifying restrictions are imposed on \(c\) and \(b(\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The allocation \((c,b(\theta))\) is not identifiable from \(r(\theta)\), because \((c+d,b(\theta)-d)\) gives the same sum for every \(d\in\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Data-generating response evaluated at the observed design points
Fitted response evaluated at the observed design points

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Taxonomy of iterative-update failures
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a nonlinear solver generate \(x_{k+1}=T_k(x_k)\) in \(\mathbb{R}^n\), with step \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) and nonnegative target measure \(R_k=R(x_k)\). Fix tolerances \(\varepsilon_R,\varepsilon_s\ge0\), a stagnation window \(q\ge1\), and a boundedness region \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic iterations, including nonstationary update maps. The labels describe observed orbit behavior and may coexist.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The iterative-update failure label set is defined by the following predicates: divergence when \(\sup_k\|x_k\|=\infty\) or \(R_k\to\infty\); nonconvergent cycling when the limit set contains more than one point and \(R_k\not\to0\); step stagnation when \(\max_{j=k-q+1,\ldots,k}\|s_j\|\le\varepsilon_s\) while \(R_k>\varepsilon_R\); residual stagnation when the relative reduction over the window is below a declared threshold while \(R_k>\varepsilon_R\); unstable amplification when nearby states or perturbations are expanded by the update dynamics; and update deterioration when an internal approximation loses a declared secant, conditioning, or regularity property. The taxonomy map returns every active label rather than forcing exclusivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The taxonomy assigns iterative-update failures using predicates on the generated orbit and its internal update model. Its classes include divergence, nonconvergent cycling, small-step stagnation away from the target, insufficient residual reduction, unstable amplification of perturbations, and deterioration of an internal secant or history approximation. More than one label may apply to the same run.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an autonomous map, a period-\(p\) cycle is a set of distinct points satisfying \(T^p(x)=x\) with \(p>1\).
Small-step stagnation is the joint condition of a small update and failure of the target measure, not merely \(\|s_k\|\) being small.
special_cases_latex: A convergent sequence with limit residual above \(\varepsilon_R\) is a non-solution stagnation outcome.
A bounded alternating two-cycle is cycling but not divergence.
immediate_consequences_latex: Step-size termination alone can incorrectly label a stagnated non-solution as successful.
Boundedness does not imply convergence because cycles and larger limit sets remain possible.
boundary_notes: Finite-window predicates are operational warnings and do not establish asymptotic behavior.
Randomized or noisy iterations require probabilistic versions of divergence, stagnation, and stability.
review_flags: The combined orbit and internal-model taxonomy has no inspected authoritative source.
Precise source support is needed for the coexistence and finite-window conventions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local and trajectory-wise instability of iteration dynamics
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable near a fixed point \(x_*\) with \(T(x_*)=x_*\). More generally, let \(x_{k+1}=T_k(x_k)\) be a differentiable nonautonomous iteration and write \(A_k=T_k'(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic differentiable dynamics. The definition covers linearized local instability and finite-horizon perturbation amplification; nonlinear global instability requires separate invariant-set analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The fixed point \(x_*\) is linearly unstable when \[\rho(T'(x_*))>1,\] where \(\rho\) is spectral radius. It is nonhyperbolic at the stability boundary when \(\rho(T'(x_*))=1\). Along a nonautonomous trajectory, the amplification from index \(j\) to \(k>j\) is \[\Phi(k,j)=A_{k-1}A_{k-2}\cdots A_j.\] The trajectory is uniformly linearly unstable on a family of horizons when \(\|\Phi(k,j)\|\) is unbounded, and it has positive upper growth rate when \[\lambda^+=\limsup_{k-j\to\infty}\frac{1}{k-j}\log\|\Phi(k,j)\|>0.\] Operational transient instability occurs when \(\|\Phi(k,j)\|\) exceeds a declared amplification threshold even if the asymptotic growth rate is nonpositive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A differentiable fixed-point iteration is linearly unstable at a fixed point when the spectral radius of its derivative exceeds one. Equality to one is a nonhyperbolic boundary rather than a stability verdict. For a changing update map, products of successive derivatives measure perturbation amplification along the trajectory. Unbounded products or a positive upper exponential growth rate define trajectory-wise instability, while a large finite product defines transient operational instability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_*\text{ is linearly unstable}\iff \rho(T'(x_*))>1,\qquad \lambda^+>0\text{ defines positive asymptotic trajectory growth}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a linear stationary iteration \(e_{k+1}=Ae_k\), the fixed point is linearly unstable when \(\rho(A)>1\).
The product \(\Phi(k,j)\) is the derivative of the composed update \(T_{k-1}\circ\cdots\circ T_j\) along the reference trajectory.
special_cases_latex: In one dimension, instability is \(|T'(x_*)|>1\).
A nonnormal product may exhibit large transient amplification even when all individual spectral radii are below one.
immediate_consequences_latex: Small perturbations can grow locally in an unstable direction.
A spectral radius equal to one requires higher-order or problem-specific analysis and is not classified as stable by this definition.
boundary_notes: Linear instability is local and does not imply every initial point diverges globally.
For nonsmooth update maps, generalized derivatives or direct metric stability notions are required.

notation.meaning: Linearized state-transition product from index j to k.

review_flags: No inspected dynamical-systems or fixed-point source supports all local, nonautonomous, and transient clauses.
A precise source locator is required before review.

children.title: Oversized-Step Failures
children.top_down_role: Covers loss of reliable progress caused by excessively large trial or accepted steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Oversized-Step Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp stability boundary for fixed-step gradient descent on a positive quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), where \(Q\succ0\) and \(L=\lambda_{\max}(Q)\). Fixed-step gradient descent satisfies
\[x_{k+1}=(I-\alpha Q)x_k.\]
It converges to the minimizer from every initialization exactly when \(0<\alpha<2/L\). If \(\alpha=2/L\) and \(x_0\) has a nonzero component in an \(L\)-eigendirection, that component alternates without decay. If \(\alpha>2/L\), its magnitude grows geometrically because \(|1-\alpha L|>1\). Thus \(2/L\) is the sharp oversized-step boundary for global linear stability on this quadratic class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For gradient descent on a positive quadratic, steps at the stability threshold cause undamped oscillation, while larger steps cause geometric divergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global convergence holds exactly for \(0<\alpha<2/L\); instability occurs for \(\alpha\ge2/L\) in an \(L\)-eigendirection.

notation.meaning: Largest eigenvalue of the quadratic Hessian

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The eigenvalue analysis and sharp fixed-step stability boundary are correct for a symmetric positive-definite quadratic, and failure_boundary is appropriate. A gradient-method source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Iteration Cycling
children.top_down_role: Covers repeated finite patterns of nonlinear iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Iteration Cycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact periodic recurrence of an iterative update without convergence to a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:X\to X\) be a deterministic iteration map on a metric space \((X,d)\). A trajectory \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\) enters a cycle of minimal period \(p\ge2\) at index \(k_0\) if
\[x_{k+p}=x_k\quad\text{for every }k\ge k_0,\qquad x_{k_0+j}\ne x_{k_0}\quad(1\le j<p).\]
The trajectory is then periodic among at least two distinct points and therefore does not converge. For example, for \(L>0\), gradient descent on \(F(x)=\tfrac12Lx^2\) with step size \(\alpha=2/L\) gives \(x_{k+1}=-x_k\), producing the two-cycle \(\{x_0,-x_0\}\) whenever \(x_0\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteration cycling is eventual periodic repetition with minimal period at least two; in a metric space such a nonconstant periodic trajectory does not converge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trajectory repeats periodically among at least two distinct points and does not converge.

notation.meaning: First index after which periodicity holds

children.title: Oscillatory Iterates
children.top_down_role: Covers alternating or fluctuating iterate behavior without stable progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Oscillatory Iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational diagnosis for bounded, nonconvergent residual-system iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), let \(x_{k+1}=T_k(x_k)\), and write \(r_k=F(x_k)\). The iterates are oscillatory if \((x_k)\) is bounded, has at least two distinct accumulation points, and fails to become asymptotically stationary: \[\limsup_{k\to\infty}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|>0.\] A finite-tail diagnostic with window \(q\ge 2\) and tolerances \(\varepsilon_x,\varepsilon_r>0\) declares oscillation when some \(j\in\{2,\ldots,q\}\) repeatedly satisfies \(\|x_k-x_{k-j}\|\le\varepsilon_x\) while \(\|r_k\|>\varepsilon_r\). Exact periodicity is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oscillation means bounded iterates repeatedly revisit separated states without settling, while the residual remains above tolerance; exact cycling is a special case, not a requirement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_k)\) exhibits nonstationary recurrent behavior with at least two accumulation points.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact sequence-level definition is mathematically meaningful, but the finite-tail diagnostic is not fully specified: “repeatedly” has no quantifier or repetition count, and the index range for feasible lags is unclear. The plain statement also describes revisiting separated states while the displayed diagnostic tests closeness to lagged states. An authoritative source is needed to select and support the intended operational criterion.

children.title: Failure-Pattern Discrimination
children.top_down_role: Covers distinctions among step overshoot, cycling, and nonperiodic oscillation.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure-Pattern Discrimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed diagnostic separating oversized steps, cycling, oscillation, and stagnation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given iterates \(x_{k-q},\ldots,x_k\), residuals \(r_i=F(x_i)\), and tolerances \(\varepsilon_s,\varepsilon_r,\varepsilon_c>0\), compute \(s_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\). Classify the tail in this order: oversized-step failure if \(\max_i\|s_i\|>\varepsilon_s\); cycling if some period \(p\ge2\) gives \(\max_i\|x_i-x_{i-p}\|\le\varepsilon_c\) and \(\min_i\|r_i\|>\varepsilon_r\); oscillation if step directions recur with sign changes and nonvanishing norms; residual stagnation if residual decrease is below its prescribed threshold; otherwise return unclassified. Output the class together with the inequalities that triggered it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate a recent iteration window and report the first quantitatively supported failure class, preserving the triggering measurements as an auditable diagnostic.
assumptions_latex: At least \(q+1\) consecutive iterates and their residuals are available.
All norms and diagnostic tolerances are fixed before classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either one supported failure label or \(\mathrm{unclassified}\), together with its numerical trigger.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate content kind, but the proposed classifier is not reproducible as written. The ranges of the maxima and minima are unspecified, admissible periods are not bounded by the window, and the oscillation and residual-stagnation tests lack quantitative predicates. Sources are required to establish the classification order and complete trigger definitions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Step-Termination Stagnation Boundary for a Residual Iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), let \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\in D\), and fix a norm, a residual tolerance \(\tau_F\geq0\), an absolute step tolerance \(\tau_a\geq0\), and a relative step tolerance \(\tau_r\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic residual iterations. This diagnostic definition concerns premature termination caused by a small computed step, not convergence established from the residual itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the scaled step threshold by \(t(x)=\tau_a+\tau_r\max\{1,\lVert x\rVert\}\). The step-termination stagnation boundary is \[\mathcal S_{\mathrm{step}}=\{(x,s)\in D\times\mathbb R^n:x+s\in D,\ \lVert s\rVert\leq t(x),\ \lVert F(x+s)\rVert>\tau_F\}.\] An iteration reaches this boundary at index \(k\) precisely when \((x_k,s_k)\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{step}}\). Thus the step test declares negligible displacement while the accepted point still fails the independently specified residual test. A stagnating run is one for which this membership occurs at one index, or repeatedly, according to the termination policy being diagnosed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a residual iteration, form the usual absolute-plus-relative step threshold. A state and proposed step lie on the step-termination stagnation boundary exactly when the step is no larger than that threshold, both the old and new points are admissible, and the residual at the new point remains above its required tolerance. Reaching this set means that a small-step stopping rule can fire without certifying a residual solution. Repeated membership may be used to classify persistent stagnation, but repetition is not required for the single-step boundary event.
assumptions_latex: The step and residual tests use the stated fixed norm and nonnegative tolerances.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\), the defining conditions are \(\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert\leq t(x_k)\) and \(\lVert F(x_{k+1})\rVert>\tau_F\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\tau_a=0\), the boundary uses the purely relative test \(\lVert s\rVert\leq\tau_r\max\{1,\lVert x\rVert\}\).
If \(s=0\) and \(\lVert F(x)\rVert>\tau_F\), then \((x,0)\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{step}}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Membership in \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{step}}\) does not certify that \(F(x+s)=0\).
A stopping rule based only on step size cannot distinguish this boundary from genuine convergence.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert why the step became small; line-search rejection, trust-region contraction, rounding, and an inaccurate model are separate mechanisms.
A point satisfying the residual tolerance is excluded even if its step is small.

notation.meaning: Set of admissible state-step pairs exhibiting small-step termination without residual success.
Combined absolute and relative step threshold.

children.title: Residual Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Covers failure of residual measures to improve materially across iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window failure to reduce the residual by more than a prescribed relative amount.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), set \(r_k=F(x_k)\). Given a window length \(q\ge 1\), residual tolerance \(\varepsilon_r>0\), and progress threshold \(\eta_r\in(0,1)\), residual stagnation at iteration \(k\ge q\) means \[\|r_k\|>\varepsilon_r\quad\text{and}\quad \|r_k\|\ge (1-\eta_r)\|r_{k-q}\|.\] Thus the residual is not acceptable and its relative reduction over the window is at most \(\eta_r\). The predicate does not by itself assert that the steps are small or that the iterates have converged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual stagnation occurs when the residual remains unacceptable and decreases by at most a prescribed relative amount over a fixed iteration window.
assumptions_latex: Residuals are evaluated using one fixed norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual has made at most the prescribed windowed progress while remaining above tolerance.

notation.meaning: Upper bound on the relative residual reduction classified as stagnation.

children.title: Step-Norm Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Covers persistently negligible iterate displacement without adequate problem resolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Step-Norm Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window persistence of small steps without an accompanying convergence claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\). Given a window length \(q\ge1\), a step threshold \(\varepsilon_s>0\), and a residual tolerance \(\varepsilon_r>0\), step-norm stagnation at iteration \(k\ge q\) means \[\max_{k-q\le i<k}\|s_i\|\le\varepsilon_s\quad\text{and}\quad \|F(x_k)\|>\varepsilon_r.\] Every recent displacement is small, but the current residual remains unacceptable. The definition deliberately separates a geometric symptom—small movement—from legitimate termination, which requires an independent residual, stationarity, or optimality test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Step-norm stagnation means all recent steps are small although the current residual is still too large to justify convergence.
assumptions_latex: Steps and residuals are measured in fixed norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Recent iterates move by at most \(\varepsilon_s\), but residual-based termination is not satisfied.

children.title: Tiny-Step False Termination
children.top_down_role: Covers premature success declarations triggered by small steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Tiny-Step False Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Small displacement alone is insufficient evidence of solving a residual system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k\ge 1\), define the accepted step \(s_k=x_k-x_{k-1}\), and suppose an implementation stops at \(x_k\) solely because \(\|s_k\|\le\varepsilon_s\). This is tiny-step false termination whenever \[\|s_k\|\le\varepsilon_s\quad\text{but}\quad \|F(x_k)\|>\varepsilon_r.\] More generally, for a constrained-optimization residual mapping \(R\), replace \(F\) by \(R\). Small steps can arise from damping, trust-region restriction, line-search rejection, ill-conditioning, or finite precision; therefore the implication \(\|s_k\|\le\varepsilon_s\Rightarrow\|F(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon_r\) is invalid without additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stopping at the current iterate only because the accepted step into it is tiny is false termination when the current residual remains above tolerance; damping or numerical restrictions can create tiny steps far from a solution.
assumptions_latex: Termination at \(x_k\) is triggered solely by the accepted-step test \(\|s_k\|\le\varepsilon_s\).
The residual and step tolerances satisfy \(\varepsilon_r>0\) and \(\varepsilon_s>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stopping decision does not certify that \(x_k\) approximately solves \(F(x)=0\).

notation.meaning: Accepted step \(x_k-x_{k-1}\) arriving at the tested iterate.

children.title: Legitimate Tiny-Step Termination
children.top_down_role: Covers regimes where a small-step signal is consistent with a credible terminal outcome.

knowledge_statements.title: Legitimate Tiny-Step Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined accepted-small-step and residual test for approximate residual-system termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(k\ge 1\), let \(s_k=x_k-x_{k-1}\) be the accepted step arriving at \(x_k\). Given \(\varepsilon_s,\varepsilon_r>0\), the pair \((x_k,s_k)\) is a legitimate tiny-step termination certificate if \[\|s_k\|\le\varepsilon_s\quad\text{and}\quad \|F(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon_r.\] The second inequality directly certifies that \(x_k\) is an \(\varepsilon_r\)-approximate zero in the chosen residual norm; the first records numerical stabilization of the iteration. For an optimization residual mapping encoding feasibility and stationarity, legitimacy additionally requires every scaled residual component to satisfy its prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tiny accepted step into the current iterate supports termination only when an independent residual test at that iterate also passes, including all required feasibility and stationarity components.
assumptions_latex: The residual mapping represents every condition required for acceptance.
Residual components and tolerances use fixed, documented scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\) is an \(\varepsilon_r\)-approximate residual-system solution, and the accepted displacement into \(x_k\) is at most \(\varepsilon_s\).

notation.meaning: Accepted step \(x_k-x_{k-1}\) arriving at the tested iterate.

knowledge_statements.title: Secant-Update Deterioration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of usefulness in an approximate Jacobian or inverse-Jacobian secant model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), \(y_k=F(x_{k+1})-F(x_k)\), and let \(B_{k+1}\) approximate the Jacobian while satisfying or approximately satisfying \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\). Secant-update deterioration is diagnosed when at least one of the following persists: \[\frac{\|B_{k+1}s_k-y_k\|}{\max\{1,\|y_k\|\}}>\tau_{\rm sec},\qquad \kappa(B_{k+1})>\kappa_{\max},\qquad \frac{\|B_{k+1}-B_k\|}{\max\{1,\|B_k\|\}}>\tau_B.\] These tests respectively indicate secant inconsistency, near-singularity, or an excessive update; any one can make the computed correction unreliable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A secant model deteriorates when it persistently violates the secant relation, becomes nearly singular, or changes excessively relative to its previous value.
assumptions_latex: The displayed matrix norms and condition number are defined consistently.
Positive diagnostic thresholds are fixed in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated linear model is not accepted as a reliable local approximation without safeguarding, resetting, or regularization.

notation.meaning: Condition number in the selected norm.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Diagnostic Secant-Update Deterioration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), let \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), \(y_k=F(x_{k+1})-F(x_k)\), and let \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) approximate a Jacobian. Fix \(\varepsilon_s,\varepsilon_y>0\) and thresholds \(\tau_{\mathrm{sec}},\tau_\kappa,\tau_\Delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional quasi-Newton or secant methods using direct Jacobian approximations. The definition is diagnostic and threshold-dependent; it does not prescribe a particular update formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lVert s_k\rVert>\varepsilon_s\) and \(\lVert y_k\rVert>\varepsilon_y\), define \[q_k=\frac{\lVert B_{k+1}s_k-y_k\rVert}{\lVert y_k\rVert},\qquad \delta_k=\frac{\lVert B_{k+1}-B_k\rVert}{\max\{1,\lVert B_k\rVert\}},\] and set \(\kappa(B)=+\infty\) when \(B\) is singular. Secant-update deterioration occurs at index \(k\) when \[q_k>\tau_{\mathrm{sec}}\quad\text{or}\quad \kappa(B_{k+1})>\tau_\kappa\quad\text{or}\quad \delta_k>\tau_\Delta.\] The three alternatives respectively identify loss of secant consistency, loss of numerical invertibility, and an update disproportionately large relative to the current model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a nontrivial displacement and residual difference, measure the updated matrix's normalized secant defect, its condition number, and the relative size of the update. The secant update is classified as deteriorated when at least one prescribed diagnostic threshold is exceeded. This covers an update that fails to reproduce the newest secant information, becomes singular or excessively ill-conditioned, or changes by an implausibly large amount relative to the preceding approximation. The definition deliberately separates deterioration from the mere fact that the matrix is inexact.
assumptions_latex: The matrix norm and its subordinate condition number are fixed consistently.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The update is not deteriorated under these diagnostics exactly when \(q_k\leq\tau_{\mathrm{sec}}\), \(\kappa(B_{k+1})\leq\tau_\kappa\), and \(\delta_k\leq\tau_\Delta\).
special_cases_latex: For an exact secant update satisfying \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\), one has \(q_k=0\); deterioration may nevertheless be detected through conditioning or update size.
If \(B_{k+1}\) is singular, then \(\kappa(B_{k+1})=+\infty\), so every finite \(\tau_\kappa\) detects deterioration.
immediate_consequences_latex: A small secant defect alone does not guarantee a stable linearized solve.
Thresholds make the classification scale-aware but method-dependent.
boundary_notes: Cases with nearly zero \(s_k\) or \(y_k\) are excluded because the normalized diagnostics become unreliable; they require a separate curvature or stagnation classification.
Inverse-Jacobian updates require the analogous defect \(\lVert H_{k+1}y_k-s_k\rVert\).

notation.meaning: Relative magnitude of the matrix update.
Set of indices classified as deteriorated.

review_flags: The supplied source hints were not inspected, so they cannot support the selected three-part diagnostic definition.
The thresholds and combined deterioration predicate require an exact scholarly locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Anderson History-Conditioning Failure
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(g:D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), let \(f_i=g(x_i)-x_i\), and at iteration \(k\) retain \(m_k\geq1\) differences \(\Delta f_i=f_{i+1}-f_i\). Write \(R_k=[\Delta f_{k-m_k},\ldots,\Delta f_{k-1}]\in\mathbb R^{n\times m_k}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Anderson acceleration formulated through a least-squares problem on residual-difference history. The definition addresses conditioning of stored history, independently of the chosen mixing parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a rank tolerance \(\tau_{\mathrm{rank}}\geq0\), a finite conditioning threshold \(\tau_\kappa\geq1\), and a coefficient threshold \(\tau_\gamma>0\). Let \(r_k=\operatorname{rank}_{\tau_{\mathrm{rank}}}(R_k)\), let \(\kappa_2(R_k)=\sigma_{\max}(R_k)/\sigma_{\min}(R_k)\) when \(R_k\) has full column rank and \(+\infty\) otherwise, and let \(\gamma_k\) be a minimum-norm solution of \(\min_\gamma\lVert f_k-R_k\gamma\rVert_2\). An Anderson history-conditioning failure occurs when \[r_k<m_k\quad\text{or}\quad\kappa_2(R_k)>\tau_\kappa\quad\text{or}\quad\lVert\gamma_k\rVert_2>\tau_\gamma.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Construct the Anderson residual-difference history matrix and solve its least-squares problem using the minimum-norm coefficient vector. History conditioning fails when the retained columns are numerically rank deficient, when their spectral condition number exceeds a prescribed threshold, or when fitting the current residual requires coefficients larger than an allowed threshold. These conditions formalize, respectively, redundant history, amplification of perturbations in the least-squares coefficients, and an unstable extrapolation even when a numerical rank decision still reports full column rank.
assumptions_latex: All retained residual vectors are available in \(\mathbb R^n\), and \(1\leq m_k\leq n\).
Numerical rank is computed using the stated singular-value tolerance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\sigma_1(R_k)\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_{m_k}(R_k)\), rank or conditioning failure is equivalent to \(\sigma_{m_k}(R_k)\leq\tau_{\mathrm{rank}}\) or \(\sigma_1(R_k)>\tau_\kappa\sigma_{m_k}(R_k)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(m_k=1\), rank failure means that the sole stored residual difference is numerically zero.
Exact duplicate or linearly dependent history columns imply \(r_k<m_k\) and \(\kappa_2(R_k)=+\infty\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Deleting dependent columns or reducing \(m_k\) changes the history matrix and may remove the defined failure.
The definition identifies instability in the acceleration subproblem, not failure of the underlying fixed-point map.
boundary_notes: Large coefficients caused solely by a deliberately tiny \(\tau_\gamma\) remain a threshold choice, not an intrinsic singularity.
Regularized Anderson variants replace the unregularized least-squares conditioning diagnostic and are outside this definition.

notation.meaning: Indices at which history conditioning fails.

review_flags: No inspected Anderson-acceleration source was supplied for the exact rank, conditioning, and coefficient thresholds.
A precise source locator is needed for this canonical-definition candidate.

children.title: Anderson Acceleration Instability
children.top_down_role: Covers unstable behavior attributable to Anderson mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Anderson Acceleration Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instability caused by unbounded or noise-amplifying Anderson mixing coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed-point map \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), define \(f_i=G(x_i)-x_i\). At iteration \(k\), let coefficients \(\alpha\) satisfy \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}\alpha=1\) and approximately minimize \(\|\sum_i\alpha_i f_i\|\) over the retained history, with update \(x_{k+1}=\sum_i\alpha_iG(x_i)\). Anderson acceleration is unstable when the mixing subproblem admits coefficients with large \(\|\alpha\|\) whose predicted residual is small but whose accepted update increases \(\|f_{k+1}\|\) or \(\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\) beyond prescribed growth factors. The mechanism is amplification of history error or evaluation noise by the coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Anderson acceleration becomes unstable when large mixing coefficients fit historical residuals but amplify errors, producing an unexpectedly large step or residual increase.
assumptions_latex: A finite Anderson history is retained.
The mixing coefficients satisfy the affine constraint \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}\alpha=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accelerated update is rejected or safeguarded because observed residual or step growth contradicts its history-based prediction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, and the Anderson formulation is recognizable, but instability is defined using unspecified prescribed growth factors and an undefined history-based prediction. No citation supports the asserted coefficient-amplification diagnostic or rejection rule.

children.title: Degenerate Residual Histories
children.top_down_role: Covers stored residual histories with insufficient independent information.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Residual Histories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank deficiency of residual differences retained by Anderson acceleration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_i=G(x_i)-x_i\), retain \(m_k\) history differences, and form \[\Delta F_k=\begin{bmatrix}f_{k-m_k+1}-f_{k-m_k}&\cdots&f_k-f_{k-1}\end{bmatrix}.\] The residual history is degenerate when \(\operatorname{rank}(\Delta F_k)<m_k\). Numerically, for a prescribed rank tolerance \(\tau_{\rm rank}>0\), it is declared degenerate when \(\sigma_{\min}(\Delta F_k)\le\tau_{\rm rank}\sigma_{\max}(\Delta F_k)\), with the zero matrix treated as degenerate. In this regime the history does not supply \(m_k\) independent residual-change directions, so the unconstrained mixing coefficients need not be uniquely or stably determined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An Anderson residual history is degenerate when its retained residual differences are linearly dependent, or numerically so according to a singular-value threshold.
assumptions_latex: The history matrix contains \(m_k\) retained residual differences.
Singular values use the Euclidean matrix norm convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained history lacks full column rank and cannot stably determine all mixing directions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the correct content kind, and exact column-rank deficiency is precise. However, the relative singular-value threshold is an uncited convention, including its treatment when the largest singular value is zero. Rank deficiency establishes nonuniqueness of the displayed least-squares parameters, but the broader claim that all mixing directions cannot be stably determined needs formulation-specific support.

children.title: Ill-Conditioned Mixing Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Covers numerical sensitivity within the coefficient-selection subproblem.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Mixing Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition-number criterion for unstable Anderson least-squares mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With Anderson residual-difference matrix \(\Delta F_k\), consider the least-squares subproblem \(\min_\gamma\|f_k-\Delta F_k\gamma\|_2\). If \(\Delta F_k\) has full column rank, the mixing problem is ill-conditioned at threshold \(\kappa_{\max}>1\) when \[\kappa_2(\Delta F_k)=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(\Delta F_k)}{\sigma_{\min}(\Delta F_k)}\ge\kappa_{\max}.\] If \(\Delta F_k\) is rank deficient, set \(\kappa_2(\Delta F_k)=+\infty\). Then small perturbations in residual evaluations can cause large changes in the least-squares coefficients, even when the minimized residual norm changes little.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Anderson mixing problem is ill-conditioned when its residual-history matrix has a large or infinite spectral condition number, making coefficients highly sensitive to perturbations.
assumptions_latex: Mixing is computed by the displayed Euclidean least-squares problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coefficient solution is potentially sensitive to small perturbations in \(f_k\) or \(\Delta F_k\).

children.title: Restart-Sensitive Behavior
children.top_down_role: Covers outcome dependence on discarding or retaining acceleration history.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart-Sensitive Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of Anderson progress on discarding and rebuilding retained history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{k+1}^{\rm keep}\) be the Anderson update using the current history and \(x_{k+1}^{\rm restart}=G(x_k)\) the depth-zero restart update from the same state. For fixed diagnostic factors \(c_r,c_s>1\), behavior is restart-sensitive at \(x_k\) when either \[\|f(x_{k+1}^{\rm keep})\|>c_r\|f(x_{k+1}^{\rm restart})\|\quad\text{or}\quad \|x_{k+1}^{\rm keep}-x_k\|>c_s\|x_{k+1}^{\rm restart}-x_k\|,\] and repeated experiments show materially different convergence after clearing the history. This property implicates retained-history geometry or conditioning rather than the current fixed-point state alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Behavior is restart-sensitive when keeping Anderson history produces substantially different residual or step growth from restarting at the same current iterate.
assumptions_latex: Both updates are evaluated from the same \(x_k\) and fixed-point map.
The comparison uses identical stopping and acceptance rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained history materially influences the next update and the subsequent convergence pattern.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Property is an appropriate role, but the record combines a one-step predicate at x_k with an unquantified requirement that repeated experiments show different subsequent convergence. The factors c_r and c_s are operational and uncited, and “materially different” has no mathematical threshold. A sourced, consistently quantified definition is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Computational Accuracy Failure Regime for Residual-System Steps
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be differentiable, and suppose an implementation uses \(\widetilde F_k=F(x_k)+e_k^F\), \(\widetilde J_k=F'(x_k)+E_k^J\), and a computed step \(s_k\) satisfying \(\widetilde J_ks_k=-\widetilde F_k+r_k^L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional residual solvers with deterministic realized error quantities. Stochastic errors may be classified after conditioning on a realization or by replacing the bounds with probabilistic ones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_k^F,a_k^J,a_k^L,a_k^R\geq0\) be the accuracy budgets for residual evaluation, derivative approximation, linearized solve, and floating-point realization. Define normalized error indicators \[\rho_k^F=\frac{\lVert e_k^F\rVert}{a_k^F},\quad \rho_k^J=\frac{\lVert E_k^J\rVert\lVert s_k\rVert}{a_k^J},\quad \rho_k^L=\frac{\lVert r_k^L\rVert}{a_k^L},\quad \rho_k^R=\frac{\lVert e_k^R\rVert}{a_k^R},\] with \(0/0=0\) and \(c/0=+\infty\) for \(c>0\). The computation is in an accuracy-failure regime at index \(k\) exactly when \[\max\{\rho_k^F,\rho_k^J,\rho_k^L,\rho_k^R\}>1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent the computed residual, Jacobian, and linearized step by exact quantities plus explicit errors, and assign a nonnegative budget to each error channel. A computational accuracy failure occurs exactly when at least one realized normalized error exceeds one: residual evaluation error, derivative error as it acts on the step, linear-solve residual, or aggregate floating-point realization error. This is an umbrella classification. Its components identify distinct mechanisms and should not be conflated merely because they produce similar outer-iteration symptoms.
assumptions_latex: The realized errors \(e_k^F\), \(E_k^J\), \(r_k^L\), and \(e_k^R\) are defined relative to stated exact-arithmetic reference quantities.
All indicators use a fixed compatible vector and operator norm.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Accuracy is adequate at index \(k\) exactly when every channel satisfies its budget: \(\lVert e_k^F\rVert\leq a_k^F\), \(\lVert E_k^J\rVert\lVert s_k\rVert\leq a_k^J\), \(\lVert r_k^L\rVert\leq a_k^L\), and \(\lVert e_k^R\rVert\leq a_k^R\).
special_cases_latex: If only residual evaluations are inexact, the predicate reduces to \(\lVert e_k^F\rVert>a_k^F\).
An exact-arithmetic exact-derivative direct solve has \(\rho_k^J=\rho_k^L=\rho_k^R=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The largest indicator identifies at least one active accuracy bottleneck.
Meeting all budgets is an accuracy condition, not by itself a convergence certificate.
boundary_notes: The budgets must be supplied by an outer accuracy policy; the definition does not determine them.
Model inadequacy of the exact linearization is not computational error and is excluded.

notation.meaning: Normalized accuracy indicators for four computational error channels.
Set of indices in a computational accuracy failure regime.

review_flags: The four-channel budget predicate is a synthesized taxonomy without an inspected exact source.
A precise authoritative locator supporting this scope and normalization is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Computational Accuracy Failure Regime for Residual-System Steps
Noisy Residual Evaluations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive deterministic or stochastic error in computed residual values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the exact residual be \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\). A noisy residual evaluation returns \[\widetilde F(x,\omega)=F(x)+e(x,\omega),\] where \(e\) is an evaluation error and \(\omega\) indexes randomness or uncontrolled computational state. Deterministic bounded noise satisfies \(\|e(x,\omega)\|\le\delta(x)\). Conditionally unbiased stochastic noise satisfies \(\mathbb E[e(x,\omega)\mid x]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[\|e(x,\omega)\|^2\mid x]\le\sigma^2(x)\). If neither condition holds, the model permits biased, state-dependent noise. Residual decreases below the local noise scale cannot be reliably distinguished from evaluation error without replication or additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noisy residual equals the exact residual plus deterministic or stochastic evaluation error; changes below the error scale are not reliably interpretable as progress.
assumptions_latex: The computed residual decomposes additively into an exact value and an error.
The selected deterministic or stochastic error bound is finite on the iterates tested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Residual differences at or below the applicable noise scale do not alone certify genuine progress.

notation.meaning: Deterministic error and stochastic standard-deviation bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Noisy Evaluation Oracle for a Residual Map
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be the target residual map, let \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\mathbb P)\) be a probability space, and let \(\widetilde F:D\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^m\) be the available evaluation oracle.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional additive evaluation noise. Both deterministic bounded errors and stochastic errors are covered, but their guarantees are stated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The oracle is a noisy residual evaluation of \(F\) when there exists an error field \(\xi:D\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^m\) such that \[\widetilde F(x,\omega)=F(x)+\xi(x,\omega)\qquad(x\in D,\ \omega\in\Omega).\] It is uniformly \(\delta\)-bounded when \(\sup_{x,\omega}\lVert\xi(x,\omega)\rVert\leq\delta\). It is conditionally unbiased with variance proxy \(\sigma^2\) when, for every queried \(x\), \(\mathbb E[\xi(x,\omega)\mid x]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[\lVert\xi(x,\omega)\rVert^2\mid x]\leq\sigma^2\). A residual test is noise-limited at \(x\) when its requested tolerance is below the applicable error scale \(\delta\) or \(\sigma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual evaluation is noisy when the value returned at a queried point equals the target residual plus an additive error. In the deterministic version, the error is bounded uniformly by a specified radius. In the stochastic version, the error has conditional mean zero and bounded conditional second moment. The evaluation becomes noise-limited when a solver asks it to resolve a residual below the corresponding error scale. The definition concerns the oracle value itself and does not assume that errors at different calls are independent.
assumptions_latex: \(\widetilde F(x,\omega)\) and \(F(x)\) belong to the same normed finite-dimensional residual space.
For the stochastic variant, \(\xi(x,\cdot)\) is measurable and square-integrable at every queried \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde F(x,\omega)-F(x)=\xi(x,\omega)\), with either \(\lVert\xi\rVert\leq\delta\) uniformly or \(\mathbb E[\xi\mid x]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[\lVert\xi\rVert^2\mid x]\leq\sigma^2\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: In the uniformly bounded case, \(F(x)\in\{y:\lVert y-\widetilde F(x,\omega)\rVert\leq\delta\}\) for every evaluation.
special_cases_latex: Deterministic inexact evaluation is recovered when \(\Omega\) is a singleton.
Exact evaluation is the case \(\xi\equiv0\), hence \(\delta=\sigma=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Uniform boundedness gives \(\bigl|\lVert\widetilde F(x,\omega)\rVert-\lVert F(x)\rVert\bigr|\leq\delta\).
A computed residual below \(\delta\) does not alone distinguish an exact root from evaluation error.
boundary_notes: Biased stochastic errors are noisy evaluations but do not satisfy the conditionally unbiased subtype.
Derivative noise produced by differencing noisy values is a separate amplified-error object.
review_flags: The additive-noise formulation is standard, but no supplied source was inspected for the exact deterministic and stochastic variants.
A precise source locator is still required by the slot contract.
knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Evaluation Oracle for a Residual Map
Derivative-Approximation Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact Newton linearization with a uniformly bounded Jacobian error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) have an \(L\)-Lipschitz Jacobian near \(x_k\), and let \(B_k=F'(x_k)+E_k\) with \(\lVert E_k\rVert\leq\varepsilon_{J,k}\). For every admissible step \(s_k\), \[\lVert F(x_k+s_k)-F(x_k)-B_ks_k\rVert\leq \frac{L}{2}\lVert s_k\rVert^2+\varepsilon_{J,k}\lVert s_k\rVert.\] Thus derivative noise dominates the quadratic Taylor error whenever \(\varepsilon_{J,k}\gtrsim L\lVert s_k\rVert\). A necessary asymptotic accuracy condition for a superlinear inexact-Newton model is \(\lVert E_ks_k\rVert=o(\lVert s_k\rVert)\); a fixed nonzero derivative-error floor generally prevents that condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jacobian error adds a first-order model defect. Once it exceeds the quadratic Taylor error, shrinking the step no longer produces an asymptotically exact Newton model.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable and \(F'\) is locally \(L\)-Lipschitz.

notation.meaning: approximate Jacobian used at iteration k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Noise in a Forward-Difference Jacobian Approximation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be differentiable, let \(\widetilde F(x)=F(x)+\xi(x)\), and suppose \(x,x+h_je_j\in D\) with \(h_j\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional forward finite differences formed from additively perturbed residual values. Other differencing formulas have analogous but different truncation orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the computed Jacobian column by \[\widetilde J_h(x)e_j=\frac{\widetilde F(x+h_je_j)-\widetilde F(x)}{h_j}.\] Its error relative to \(F'(x)e_j\) decomposes exactly as \[\widetilde J_h(x)e_j-F'(x)e_j=t_j(h_j)+n_j(h_j),\] where \[t_j(h_j)=\frac{F(x+h_je_j)-F(x)}{h_j}-F'(x)e_j,\qquad n_j(h_j)=\frac{\xi(x+h_je_j)-\xi(x)}{h_j}.\] Derivative-approximation noise is the term \(n_j(h_j)\); the approximation is noise-dominated when \(\lVert n_j(h_j)\rVert>\lVert t_j(h_j)\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forward-difference Jacobian made from noisy residual values has two distinct errors. The truncation term is the error that would remain with exact residual evaluations. The derivative-noise term is the difference of the two evaluation errors divided by the finite-difference step. Derivative-approximation noise is precisely this latter term, and the column is called noise-dominated when its norm exceeds the truncation-error norm. This definition makes explicit that decreasing the differencing step can amplify evaluation noise even while reducing truncation error.
assumptions_latex: The two residual evaluations exist, and \(h_j\neq0\).
\(F\) is differentiable at \(x\); a quantitative truncation bound additionally requires local derivative regularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(n_j(h_j)=[\xi(x+h_je_j)-\xi(x)]/h_j\), and noise domination means \(\lVert n_j(h_j)\rVert>\lVert t_j(h_j)\rVert\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If each evaluation error satisfies \(\lVert\xi(\cdot)\rVert\leq\delta\), then \(\lVert n_j(h_j)\rVert\leq2\delta/|h_j|\).
special_cases_latex: With exact residual evaluations, \(\xi\equiv0\) and hence \(n_j(h_j)=0\).
If identical additive error affects both evaluations, then it cancels and \(n_j(h_j)=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Arbitrarily small \(|h_j|\) need not improve \(\widetilde J_h(x)e_j\) when the error difference is nonzero.
Residual noise is amplified by the factor \(1/|h_j|\) in a forward difference.
boundary_notes: Cancellation, correlation, and stochastic independence of evaluation errors affect probabilistic bounds but not the defining decomposition.
Complex-step and automatic-differentiation errors are outside this forward-difference definition.

notation.meaning: Evaluation-noise contribution to the computed derivative column.

review_flags: The exact algebraic decomposition is well specified, but the hinted finite-difference sources were not inspected.
The requested precise supporting locator is absent.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linearized-Solve Accuracy Mismatch
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), let \(J_k\) be the matrix used at \(x_k\), and let the computed step satisfy \(J_ks_k=-F(x_k)+r_k\). Define \(\eta_k=\lVert r_k\rVert/\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\) when \(F(x_k)\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional inexact Newton-type steps. The definition distinguishes under-solving from wasteful over-solving relative to an outer iteration's requested forcing level and attainable accuracy floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0\leq\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}<1\) be the largest relative linear residual allowed by the outer method, and let \(0\leq\eta_k^{\mathrm{floor}}\leq\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}\) be the estimated attainable or useful lower level imposed by data, matrix, and arithmetic errors. A linearized-solve accuracy mismatch occurs when \[\eta_k>\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}\quad\text{or}\quad\eta_k<\eta_k^{\mathrm{floor}}.\] The first alternative is under-solving: the step does not meet the outer forcing requirement. The second is over-solving: the inner iteration resolves the stated linear model more accurately than the model and computational data justify.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measure the residual of the computed linearized equation relative to the current nonlinear residual. The outer solver supplies the largest acceptable forcing ratio, while an accuracy model supplies a lower floor below which further inner accuracy is not useful or reliably measurable. A mismatch occurs if the achieved ratio lies above the upper requirement or below the lower floor. The two cases distinguish inadequate linear solves from excessive inner work; an achieved ratio inside the closed interval is matched to the stated outer and computational accuracy scales.
assumptions_latex: \(F(x_k)\neq0\), so the relative linear residual is defined.
The requested forcing level and attainable floor satisfy \(0\leq\eta_k^{\mathrm{floor}}\leq\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}<1\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Accuracy matching holds exactly when \(\eta_k^{\mathrm{floor}}\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\leq\lVert J_ks_k+F(x_k)\rVert\leq\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\eta_k^{\mathrm{floor}}=0\), only under-solving is classified as a mismatch.
An exact linear solve has \(\eta_k=0\); it is over-solved whenever \(\eta_k^{\mathrm{floor}}>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The interval \([\eta_k^{\mathrm{floor}},\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}]\) is the matched-accuracy regime.
A small linear residual does not correct an inaccurate Jacobian or residual evaluation.
boundary_notes: When \(F(x_k)=0\), the nonlinear problem already satisfies the exact residual equation and this relative diagnostic is unnecessary.
The lower floor is policy-dependent; without a justified floor, over-solving cannot be certified.

notation.meaning: Achieved relative residual of the linearized solve.
Outer method's maximum permitted forcing ratio.
Estimated useful or attainable lower accuracy level.

review_flags: The under-solving predicate is standard, but the combined lower-floor mismatch definition lacks an inspected source.
A locator supporting both under-solving and over-solving is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Oversolved Linearized Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-solve accuracy below the trustworthy residual-model floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x_k\), suppose an inexact Newton step satisfies \(F(x_k)+B_ks_k=r_k\), while residual and linearization uncertainties imply that the computable linearized residual is uncertain by at most \(\delta_k>0\). The solve is oversolved when \[\lVert r_k\rVert\ll\delta_k.\] Reducing \(\lVert r_k\rVert\) further cannot certify a smaller true linearized defect than order \(\delta_k\), because the latter is bounded by \(\lVert r_k\rVert+\delta_k\). A noise-aware termination rule therefore stops the inner solve once \(\lVert r_k\rVert\leq c\delta_k\) for a fixed moderate \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linearized system is oversolved when its algebraic residual is much smaller than uncertainty in the residual or Jacobian, so extra inner iterations provide no certifiable accuracy.
assumptions_latex: The discrepancy between computed and true linearized defects is bounded by \(\delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert r_k\rVert\ll\delta_k\) identifies oversolving, and \(\lVert r_k\rVert\leq c\delta_k\) is a noise-aware stopping threshold.

notation.meaning: algebraic residual of the linearized solve
aggregate uncertainty in the linearized residual

knowledge_statements.title: Undersolved Linearized Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact Newton forcing residual too large for the requested local rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x_*)=0\), let \(F'(x_*)\) be nonsingular, and compute \(s_k\) from \[F(x_k)+F'(x_k)s_k=r_k,\qquad \lVert r_k\rVert\leq\eta_k\lVert F(x_k)\rVert.\] Locally, \(\lVert F(x_{k+1})\rVert=O(\eta_k\lVert F(x_k)\rVert+\lVert F(x_k)\rVert^2)\). Hence a bound \(\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\) supports local linear contraction, whereas superlinear convergence requires \(\eta_k\to0\). Relative to either requirement, the system is undersolved when the attained forcing factor violates it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner solve is undersolved when its forcing residual is too large for contraction or for the requested superlinear outer convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) has a locally Lipschitz Jacobian near a root \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert F(x_{k+1})\rVert=O(\eta_k\lVert F(x_k)\rVert+\lVert F(x_k)\rVert^2)\), so superlinear convergence requires \(\eta_k\to0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Forcing-Accuracy Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility interval between outer convergence demands and an inner accuracy floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an inexact Newton equation, let \(\eta_k\) satisfy \(\lVert r_k\rVert\leq\eta_k\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\). Suppose uncertainty imposes the attainable lower bound \(\lVert r_k\rVert\geq\delta_k\), while the desired outer convergence rate requires \(\eta_k\leq\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}\). The two requirements are compatible exactly when \[\frac{\delta_k}{\lVert F(x_k)\rVert}\leq\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}.\] A forcing-accuracy mismatch occurs when this interval is empty, equivalently when \(\delta_k>\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\). No choice of inner stopping tolerance can then satisfy both attainability and the requested outer accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forcing accuracy is mismatched when the smallest attainable inner residual already exceeds the largest residual allowed by the desired outer convergence rate.
assumptions_latex: The attainable linear-solve residual has lower bound \(\delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_k>\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\) if and only if no admissible forcing factor exists.

notation.meaning: largest forcing factor allowed by the requested outer rate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compatibility interval is internally consistent and the condition content kind fits the exact leaf, but no source is supplied for the residual-floor model or its connection to the requested outer convergence rate.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Loss of Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Roundoff ambiguity in acceptance, decrease, and positivity tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a safeguard accept a trial step when \(a_k-\rho_{\min}p_k\geq 0\), where \(a_k\) and \(p_k>0\) are the exact actual and predicted decreases. Suppose floating-point evaluations satisfy \(\lvert\widehat a_k-a_k\rvert\leq\epsilon_{a,k}\) and \(\lvert\widehat p_k-p_k\rvert\leq\epsilon_{p,k}\). Then the computed test has the same sign as the exact test whenever \[\lvert a_k-\rho_{\min}p_k\rvert>\epsilon_{a,k}+\rho_{\min}\epsilon_{p,k}.\] Inside the complementary band, the stated error bounds do not certify the decision sign, so rounding can reverse acceptance or rejection unless higher precision, interval bounds, or a widened decision margin is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A safeguard can be reversed by rounding when its exact decision margin is no larger than the accumulated error bound for the actual and predicted decreases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The error bounds certify the safeguard's sign if \(\lvert a_k-\rho_{\min}p_k\rvert>\epsilon_{a,k}+\rho_{\min}\epsilon_{p,k}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Precision Loss of a Numerical Safeguard
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a safeguard accept a trial object \(z\in D\) exactly when a real-valued margin \(\phi(z)\leq0\). Suppose floating-point computation returns \(\widehat\phi(z)=\phi(z)+e_\phi(z)\) with a certified bound \(|e_\phi(z)|\leq\epsilon_\phi(z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-precision evaluation of scalar acceptance predicates, including line-search, trust-region, feasibility, and denominator safeguards.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The safeguard is numerically resolved at \(z\) when \(|\widehat\phi(z)|>\epsilon_\phi(z)\), because the error interval \(I(z)=[\widehat\phi(z)-\epsilon_\phi(z),\widehat\phi(z)+\epsilon_\phi(z)]\) lies strictly on one side of zero. Finite-precision loss of the safeguard occurs when \[0\in I(z),\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad |\widehat\phi(z)|\leq\epsilon_\phi(z).\] In this regime the computed sign of the acceptance margin is not certified: admissible roundoff errors include values for which the exact predicate accepts and values for which it rejects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Express a safeguard as the sign test on an exact scalar margin and bound the error in the computed margin. The safeguard is lost to finite precision exactly when the resulting uncertainty interval contains zero. Equivalently, the magnitude of the computed margin is no larger than its certified error bound. At such a point the floating-point comparison cannot certify the exact accept-or-reject decision, because both signs are compatible with the error model. This definition concerns loss of decisiveness, whether or not the implemented comparison happens to return the correct Boolean value.
assumptions_latex: The exact safeguard can be represented by \(\phi(z)\leq0\).
The forward-error bound \(|\widehat\phi(z)-\phi(z)|\leq\epsilon_\phi(z)\) is valid and \(\epsilon_\phi(z)\geq0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Loss occurs exactly when the error model permits two margins \(a\leq0<b\) consistent with the same computed value.
special_cases_latex: If \(\epsilon_\phi(z)=0\), loss occurs only at \(\widehat\phi(z)=0\).
For a strict-positivity denominator safeguard \(d(z)>0\), take \(\phi(z)=-d(z)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\widehat\phi(z)<-\epsilon_\phi(z)\), acceptance is certified.
If \(\widehat\phi(z)>\epsilon_\phi(z)\), rejection is certified.
boundary_notes: An incorrect decision outside the interval model indicates an invalid error bound or another defect, not the defined ambiguity.
Overflow, underflow to zero, and invalid values require extended arithmetic models unless incorporated into \(\epsilon_\phi\).

notation.meaning: Certified interval containing the exact safeguard margin.
Set on which finite precision makes the safeguard undecidable under the error model.

review_flags: The interval-sign formulation is mathematically precise but was not matched to an inspected source locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure Boundary of a One-Parameter Continuation Problem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G:U\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable, write \(z=(x,\lambda)\), and let \(\mathcal C\) be a connected one-dimensional component of \(G^{-1}(0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic continuation of a one-dimensional zero set. The definition separates intrinsic geometric boundaries from failures of a particular predictor-corrector implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The regular continuation region is \[\mathcal R=\{z\in\mathcal C\cap U:\operatorname{rank}DG(z)=n\}.\] Its intrinsic continuation failure boundary is \[\partial_{\mathcal C}\mathcal R=\overline{\mathcal R}^{\,\mathcal C}\setminus\operatorname{int}_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal R).\] A point \(z_*\in\overline{\mathcal C}\) is additionally an escape boundary when either \(z_*\in\partial U\), or a sequence \(z_j\in\mathcal C\) has no finite accumulation point while approaching the end of the selected continuation interval. Thus continuation encounters a failure boundary when regular local path structure is lost, the modeled domain is reached, or the component escapes every bounded subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a one-parameter residual equation, the regular continuation region consists of solution points where the full derivative with respect to state and parameter has maximal row rank. The intrinsic failure boundary is the relative boundary of this regular subset within the selected connected solution component. Domain-boundary points and unbounded escape of the component are also continuation failure boundaries. This definition concerns the geometry and domain of the exact zero set; a corrector that fails at an otherwise regular interior point is an algorithmic failure rather than an intrinsic boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is continuously differentiable on the open set \(U\).
\(\mathcal C\) is the selected connected one-dimensional solution component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_*\) is an intrinsic failure-boundary point when \(z_*\in\partial_{\mathcal C}\mathcal R\), \(z_*\in\overline{\mathcal C}\cap\partial U\), or the selected component escapes without a finite accumulation point.
equivalent_formulations_latex: At an interior solution point, failure of regularity is \(\operatorname{rank}DG(z_*)<n\).
special_cases_latex: A fold in the parameter projection may have singular \(G_x\) while \(DG=[G_x\ G_\lambda]\) retains rank \(n\); it is therefore not intrinsically singular for arclength continuation.
If \(\mathcal C\) is compact and contained in \(U\), escape boundaries are absent.
immediate_consequences_latex: Parameter continuation can fail at a fold even though pseudo-arclength continuation remains in \(\mathcal R\).
A regular interior point cannot be an intrinsic rank-failure boundary.
boundary_notes: Branch switching is a selection failure near a multi-branch solution set and is classified separately.
Corrector divergence caused by poor step size does not establish an intrinsic failure boundary.

notation.meaning: Maximal-row-rank portion of the selected solution component.
Boundary of the regular region relative to the solution component.

review_flags: No inspected continuation reference supports the combined rank, domain, and escape-boundary definition.
A precise continuation-theory source locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simple Fold and Parameter-Turning Regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G:U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n\) be twice continuously differentiable and let \(z_*=(x_*,\lambda_*)\in U\) satisfy \(G(z_*)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional one-parameter continuation near a simple fold. The full solution curve remains regular for pseudo-arclength parameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The point \(z_*\) is a simple fold with respect to \(\lambda\) when \[\operatorname{rank}G_x(z_*)=n-1,\qquad \operatorname{rank}[G_x(z_*)\ \ G_\lambda(z_*)]=n,\] and, for nonzero right and left null vectors \(v\in\ker G_x(z_*)\) and \(w\in\ker G_x(z_*)^T\), \[w^TG_\lambda(z_*)
eq0,
\qquad w^TG_{xx}(z_*)[v,v]
eq0.\] A continuation curve \(z(s)=(x(s),\lambda(s))\) through \(z_*\) is in a fold-turning regime when \(\lambda'(s_*)=0\), \(x'(s_*)
eq0\), and \(\lambda'\) changes sign across \(s_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simple fold is a solution where the state Jacobian loses exactly one rank, while the derivative with respect to both state and continuation parameter retains maximal row rank. The parameter derivative must be transverse to the left nullspace, and the second state derivative along the right-null direction must be nonzero. Along a regular arclength parameterization, the state tangent is nonzero while the parameter tangent vanishes and reverses sign. Ordinary parameter continuation encounters a turning point there, although pseudo-arclength continuation can traverse the regular full solution curve.
assumptions_latex: The left and right nullspaces of \(G_x(z_*)\) are one-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated rank, transversality, and nondegeneracy conditions define a simple fold, with \(\lambda'(s_*)=0\) and parameter reversal along its regular local solution curve.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The full derivative has maximal row rank while the projection \((x,\lambda)\mapsto\lambda\) restricted to the solution curve has a nondegenerate critical point.
special_cases_latex: For \(n=1\), the conditions reduce to \(G_x=0\), \(G_\lambda\neq0\), and \(G_{xx}\neq0\) at the solution.
A vertical tangent in an \(x\)-versus-\(\lambda\) plot is compatible with a regular arclength tangent.
immediate_consequences_latex: The implicit-function representation \(x=x(\lambda)\) generally fails at the fold.
The full zero set remains locally one-dimensional because \([G_x\ G_\lambda]\) has row rank \(n\).
boundary_notes: If the second-order nondegeneracy vanishes, the point is a higher-order degeneracy rather than a simple fold.
A fold is not by itself a branch point.

notation.meaning: Nonzero right-null vector of the singular state Jacobian.
Nonzero left-null vector of the singular state Jacobian.

review_flags: The simple-fold conditions are standard but lack an inspected source in the supplied evidence set.
A precise continuation or bifurcation-theory locator is required.
